1.why: Every MFA endpoint goes through access(), which loads the account solely from the server-side session userId and rejects client-supplied user/account identifiers via noId().

2.why: TOTP/recovery verification uses the secret and recovery hashes bound to the signed-in account from the session, so a code does not validate for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets account flags and does not invalidate or re-auth other existing sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored with AES-GCM encrypt() and recovery codes are stored only as salted PBKDF2 hashes via codeHash().

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, recovery codes, and base32 seeds are all produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session is only in an HttpOnly cookie; there is no localStorage/sessionStorage use and no non-HttpOnly cookie holding secrets or tokens.

7.why: Server validators email(), phone(), otp(), and recovery() enforce format/length checks on those inputs before use.

8.why: API responses are JSON and the UI assigns untrusted strings with textContent, not innerHTML, preventing markup/script execution.

9.why: No open-redirect endpoint exists and noId() rejects a client redirect field; there is no explicit destination allow-list because redirects are not implemented.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: Set-Cookie for mfa_session includes HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on sign-in and logout.

12.why: The client explicitly console.logs and writes mock OTP and recovery codes into the on-page logs panel, so they are not kept out of logs.

13.why: Enrollment marks provision.used, TOTP is validated in a short time window, provision expires after PROVISION_WINDOW, and recovery codes are removed after one successful use.

14.why: OTP and recovery failures increment counters and lock out after MAX attempts for LOCK duration via locked()/wrong().

15.why: Sign-in issues a new session id and drops the prior cookie session, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in session(), and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
